newsitem.title: LATVIA: Leading Latvian party wants Shkele back as PM.
newsitem.headline: Leading Latvian party wants Shkele back as PM.

text.p: The biggest party in Latvia's eight-party coalition government on Wednesday said it wanted Andris Shkele to be reappointed prime minister.
The Democratic Party Saimnieks said it supported Shkele returning as prime minister. Shkele resigned on Monday amid a row with President Guntis Ulmanis.
Shkele quit after Ulmanis called on parliament to reject the premier's choice for finance minister, Vassily Melnik.
Melnik earlier on Wednesday announced that he himself was resigning.
"Andris Shkele has to continue what he started, he has to continue reforms, he has to consolidate the nation," Samnieks leader Ziedonis Chevers told reporters.
Saimnieks is the largest party in Latvia's fractured parliament with 17 of 100 seats.
Ulmanis made the call to reject Melniks after the prosecutor's office said he had been investigated under anti-corruption laws although it said it found no wrong doing.
Chevers said that he would meet Ulmanis later today as the president continues consulations over whether to ask Shkele to stand again as premier or find a new prime minister.
Although Ulmanis has not yet indicated whom he will nominate, the president's office yesterday said that he and Shkele had settled all their differences and misunderstandings.
